newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin sees good Bonn ties whoever wins in France.
newsitem.headline: Jospin sees good Bonn ties whoever wins in France.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin, a likely prime minister if the left wins a parliamentary election runoff on Sunday, said on Friday he expected good relations with Germany whoever was in power in Paris.

Jospin was asked in a France-Info radio interview about his relations with conservative Chancellor Helmut Kohl. He replied: "There are elections in Germany too. Mr Kohl is a wise man, a European who knows that whatever the government in France, relations between France and Germany must be good."

Jospin said he had received messages from several European leaders, mainly socialists or social democrats, ahead of Sunday's decisive second round of voting, which the left-wing opposition is favourite to win.
Reuters erroneously reported that he included Kohl among those who had sent him messages. It was the interviewer who mentioned Kohl's name and Jospin did not reply.

"To reduce the 15-nation European Union to a Franco-German duo or a duel is to make a political mistake towards the other major partners, such as Britain, at a time when it is returning towards Europe, Spain, Italy and numerous other great nations which don't want to see Europe reduced to a duo," Jospin said.

On a visit to Paris last week, Kohl said he trusted the wisdom of French voters. But he also said he saw no reason to renegotiate the terms for a single European currency, as Jospin has suggested the Socialists would seek to do.
